issue_paraphrase: A character set expressed as a complement - 'every character except those in [a, b]' - is mishandled by a containment query in a character-range utility. When the excluded segment touches the start or end of the whole character domain, the complement collapses to a trivial set (the empty set, everything from a boundary on, or everything up to a boundary), and the utility answers that a plain range does not contain it even when it logically does. Only ranges that explicitly span the entire domain get the right answer; subset checks at the domain bounds return false incorrectly.
fix_summary: CharRange.contains(CharRange) gained handling for the boundary cases of a negated argument range: an excluded range covering [0, MAX_VALUE] denotes the empty set (always contained), an excluded range starting at 0 leaves a single high interval, and one ending at MAX_VALUE leaves a single low interval; containment is then decided by interval comparison instead of the previous blanket answer which only accepted ranges spanning the full domain.
notes: Pure-logic fix, no network at test time (maven needs network only for first dependency download). One mvn test run at 1 CPU takes ~1.5-3 min (full recompile on first visit to a commit; only changed files after that). CharRange is package-private, so any direct repro main must be placed in package org.apache.commons.lang3. Golden test text is the one the fix commit itself added; at the parent it must be overlayed from the fix commit because the method does not exist there.

issue_paraphrase: Multiplying two fractions throws an arithmetic overflow error even when the correct result fits comfortably in a 32-bit int, whenever either operand has not been reduced to lowest terms. The library cancels common factors only across the two operands and assumes both are already reduced, so a fraction like 100/1000000 (one hundredth of one hundredth... i.e. 1/10000) combined with a fraction whose denominator is close to the int limit overflows an intermediate product that the reduced result would never need. Callers get a spurious ArithmeticException from a perfectly valid computation; division and power operations route through the same code path.
fix_summary: Fraction.multiplyBy now reduces both operands into locals first (greatestCommonDivisor of each numerator/denominator pair) before applying the Knuth 4.5.1 cross-gcd cancellation, so an internal factor shared inside a single operand cannot overflow the intermediate int products. Added regression assertions for multiply and divide using 100/1000000 with denominator 46341, asserting the exact reduced results.
notes: Pure-logic fix, no network at test time. Uses the public org.apache.commons.lang3.math.Fraction API. One mvn run at 1 CPU ~1.5-3 min. Golden method names: the new asserts live in testMultiply (multiply case) and testDivide (divideBy case); testMultiply alone is sufficient as the regression signal. The same class later received a follow-up fix for add/subtract (#1784) - do not mix the two; they are independent commits.

issue_paraphrase: Padding a string to a very large target size can exhaust the Java heap and kill the whole process instead of returning the input unchanged. Passing Integer.MIN_VALUE as the desired length makes the padding routines subtract the current string length from that minimum int, which overflows into a huge positive pad count; the code then attempts to materialize a multi-gigabyte character array and the JVM dies with an OutOfMemoryError that no application code can catch. Any server that pads values based on untrusted lengths crashes outright, where a size no larger than the string's own length should simply be a no-op returning the original string.
fix_summary: leftPad and rightPad (both the char-padChar and String-padStr overloads) now return the input string immediately when the requested size is not greater than the current string length, so the pad-count arithmetic can never overflow into a giant allocation. Previously only the str == null case was short-circuited. Added regression asserts calling leftPad("abc", Integer.MIN_VALUE, ...) and rightPad(...) expecting the string unchanged.
notes: DoS/OOM class bug, very user-visible, public StringUtils API. The parent-side failure is an uncaught OutOfMemoryError that crashes the fork, which makes the golden test run report a surefire dump + mvn exit 1 rather than an ordinary assertion failure - do not mistake that for an environment problem. Keep the direct repro under -Xmx256m so the OOM is fast and deterministic. The `mvn test-compile` before the direct repro builds target/classes for the checkout being tested. Test runs are offline; only the first maven invocation needs network.
